newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Amoco finances Kazakh share of CPC pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Amoco finances Kazakh share of CPC pipeline.

text.p: Amoco Corp signed a $150 million deal with Kazakhstan's state oil company here on Wednesday to help finance the country's stake in the Caspian Pipeline Consortium pipeline project.
Amoco will pay for Kazakhstan's 19 percent share in the $1.5-$2.0 billion Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC), which plans to build a major oil export pipeline.
In return the U.S. oil major will have the right to export 60,000 barrels per day of crude to Russia's Black Sea outlet of Novorossiisk via the link once it is built.
"Amoco will have the right to ship three million tonnes a year on the pipeline," President of Amoco Eurasia Petroleum Ltd T. Don Stacey told reporters. "I think it's a good deal."
Amoco does not have a formal equity stake in CPC.

It is one of three shortlisted finalists in a tender for Kazakhstan's giant Uzen oil field, the result of which is due later this month, and is eyeing other regional energy projects for which export capacity will be crucial.
"We've found a partner who will pay for our share in the construction in the pipeline, who will share with us our quota," Kazakh Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin told a signing ceremony.
He underlined the pipeline's importance in bringing the landlocked former Soviet republic closer to world markets.

The CPC comprises eight international oil companies and the states of Russia, Kazakhstan and Oman in a project to build a $1.5 billion pipeline to export oil, first from Kazakhstan's rich Tengiz oil field, to western markets.

CPC includes Chevron Corp with 15 percent, Russia's LUKoil with 12.5 percent, Mobil Corp and Russia's Rosneft with 7.5 percent each, British Gas Plc and Italy's Agip SpA with two percent each while Kazakh Oil (which now has Kazakh Munaigaz's stake) and Oryx Energy Company have 1.75 percent each.
The remaining 50 percent is divided between Russia with 24 percent, Kazakhstan, with 19 percent, and Oman, through the Oman Oil Company, with seven percent.
CPC says the proposed 1,580 km (990 mile) pipeline could eventually carry 1.4 million barrels per day and hopes to start and complete the link by 2000, but the project is behind schedule.
